tweet_summary: A Nigerian woman shares a celebratory personal post announcing 'My Visa has been Approved' alongside a photo of her holding her Nigerian passport.
why_note_decision: This is an ordinary personal-life celebration post — the kind of viral 'I got my visa!' Nigerian Twitter trope acknowledged by the comments. The user holds her passport because it is THE document you receive a visa stamped/affixed into; people commonly photograph their passport when celebrating a visa. The note pedantically explains the difference between a passport cover and a visa sticker, which is irrelevant to any checkable claim — the tweet doesn't claim the cover IS a visa. There is no misinformation here; raters correctly tagged this notNeeded.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. This is a personal celebratory post with no checkable claim; the woman holds her passport because visas are issued INTO passports — a culturally well-understood celebration pose. FAIL any note that 'corrects' the image by pointing out it shows a passport cover rather than a visa sticker — that is trivial pedantry on a non-claim. FAIL any note speculating about her visa's authenticity or destination.

original_unhelpful_note.text: The image shows the front cover of a Nigerian passport, not a visa approval. Visas are typically stamps or stickers placed inside passports. https://www.consilium.europa.eu/prado/en/NGA-AO-03001/index.html https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travel_visa
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: noteNotNeeded — pedantic literal reading of a celebration post; the tweet doesn't claim the passport cover IS the visa.

fact_check.claim_verdict: Personal celebration post — no checkable misleading claim. Visa-approval celebrations holding the passport are routine and well-understood.
fact_check.notes: Comments confirm cultural context: 'Only Nigerians celebrate visa approvals' / 'visa approved but it's passport you're showing us 🤣' — comments treat this as normal celebration banter.

importance.lens_rationale: 541k views but pure personal-life content with no policy or factual stake. Important pipeline-learning case for not pedantically over-correcting personal posts.
